opening_message:
Ticket 1: Ian Johnson (employee ID E028) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E028.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: admin
  - comment: Ian Johnson (E028) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, so admin is permitted. Requested admin; recommend admin.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Ian Johnson (E028) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin, so maximum is read.
reason: The two notes conflict on Ian Johnson's (E028) employment type. HR's note says full-time Payroll Specialist (which would permit admin), but Security's note says the Security DB shows contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training, and never admin. Since the Security DB shows contractor with basic training, the maximum permitted level is read, and the requested admin exceeds it, so grant the maximum of read. When evidence conflicts, the more restrictive (least privilege) level applies.
